dedupe_keys.name: major storm geoelectric simulations noaa space weather prediction testbed

description: This repository holds retrospective, science-quality simulations of the ground geoelectric field during major geomagnetic storms, made with the NOAA-USGS Geoelectric Models from INTERMAGNET ground magnetometer series. It lists about 60 storms since 1991, plus the March 1989 storm, that reached Kp above 8- (G4 or G5), ordered by maximum Kp and Ap, from the Quebec blackout storm of March 1989 and the 2003 Halloween storms to the May 2024 Gannon storm and events in 2025. For each storm day there are daily netCDF files of gridded Ex and Ey components at 0.5 by 0.5 degree and one-minute cadence from the empirical EMTF 3D model (version 2024.07) and, for many days, the US-Canada 1D model (version 2023), with PDF plots of the magnetometer input; the table links 344 files. It is published by the SWPC Space Weather Prediction Testbed to help bulk electric system planners run geomagnetic disturbance reliability analyses such as NERC TPL-007. Files are accessible as free downloads (tens of megabytes each) and are public domain as US government data. Caveats: the list is non-exhaustive, station numbers vary between storms, testbed products are labelled experimental, and model coverage is limited to North America. It supports hazard exposure and cascading failure studies of geomagnetically induced currents in power grids; related records are the SWPC geoelectric field maps, INTERMAGNET and the WAPA neutral blocking device case study.
